intuition: Carry the values along the current route from the root. At a leaf, join those values into a path string and save it. Remove the current value when returning to the parent so that another branch starts with the right ancestor path.

Maintain one path list for the current recursive branch. A node is appended on entry, and removed after its descendants finish. Only a node with neither child completes a requested path. Joining the list at that moment captures a stable string before backtracking changes working storage.

A node with one child must continue downward; stopping there would report an internal prefix rather than a root-to-leaf path. Output strings can repeat when distinct leaves have equal value sequences, and those occurrences must be preserved.

On entering a node, path contains exactly its ancestors. Appending the current value creates its complete root path. Only leaves produce results, and DFS reaches each leaf once. Popping restores the ancestor path for sibling exploration, so all and only root-to-leaf paths are emitted.
L is the total number of characters in all returned paths; joining at leaves accounts for output size.

steps: Descend left to 2, then its right child 5, producing ["1","2","5"].
Pop 5 and 2 while returning, leaving the root path ["1"].
Visit right leaf 3 and record "1->3"; return both strings.

codeNotes.note: Both child pointers must be absent; a one-child node is an internal node, not a completed path.
Joining copies the current branch into an immutable result string before sibling traversal changes the list.
Undo this node’s append so the next sibling inherits exactly the parent path, without leftover values.

keyDecision: Save paths only at leaves. Undo the appended value after exploring the node.
